question: On how many of the two trading days October 15–16, 2026 will US spot Bitcoin ETFs record a net daily inflow?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: daily sign of the aggregate US spot BTC ETF flow. Over the 21 trading days from Sep 4 to Oct 5, 2026, 13 were positive (about 62%). Since launch the share has been roughly 55-60%, and H1 2026 had net outflows, so I use a marginal p(positive) of about 0.58. Signs cluster: there was a 9-day inflow streak followed by mixed days, so after a positive day the chance of another positive day is about 0.68. That gives P(both positive) ≈ 0.39, P(neither) ≈ 0.24 and P(exactly one) ≈ 0.37. Q3 inflows were strong ($6.3B) but have cooled: Sep 30 was -148.7, Oct 1 +102.7, Oct 2 +189.8 and Oct 5 -89.9. No human market was found: the harness search found nothing on Polymarket or Manifold, and my web search found no ETF-flow contract on Kalshi or with bookmakers.

The Q3 2026 regime leaned toward inflows ($3.5B in Aug, $2.7B in Sep; 8 of the last 10 days positive per Bitbo through Oct 2). Early October is mixed: +102.7M (Oct 1), +189.9M (Oct 2), -89.9M (Oct 5), 0 (Oct 6), with BTC stalling near $86k. Per-day positive probability is about 0.58, and positive correlation between consecutive days fattens the 0 and 2 outcomes: P(0)≈0.23, P(1)≈0.39, P(2)≈0.38. calls.reasoning: Per-day P(Farside Total>0) ~0.58: 13/21 sessions positive Sep 4-Oct 5 2026 (62%, inflated by a 9-day streak), long-run ~55-60%, H1 2026 net outflows, early Oct mixed (+102.7, +189.8, -89.9). Signs cluster, so the 0 and 2 outcomes get more weight than independent days would give: P0~0.25, P1~0.36, P2~0.39. Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the data (21-session sign count, monthly flows, early-Oct prints) and on a per-day p of about 0.57-0.58 with positive autocorrelation. The only disputes were small factual ones (Oct 2 +189.8 vs +189.9; Oct 6 reported as 0, probably an incomplete report; Bitbo vs Farside discrepancies). None of them change the estimate. I kept p=0.58 and P(+|+)~0.68, giving a P0/P1/P2 split close to Run 1's; that is where the evidence sits, not a split-the-difference. The CPI date for Oct 15-16 was not verified by any run and could not be settled without web access; it adds variance but no direction.
